messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert triggered — runtime-serving (eu-west) — symptom=rapid OOMs + autoscaler oscillation. Observed: burst of CUDA OOMs -> pods CrashLoopBackOff -> autoscaler scales up -> new pods hit same OOM -> nodes saturated -> autoscaler scales down -> brownout. Start 2025-11-12T02:14:36Z. Paging oncall-sre.
Maya R: on it. I’m the oncall. reading logs now. paging infra and runtime teams. :raised_hand:
Jia Chen: giving logs I pulled from the runtime cluster, snippets:
```
[2025-11-12T02:14:21Z] model-runner-abcde kubelet: Pod crashed: terminationMessage=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2025-11-12T02:14:22Z] liveness probe failed => CrashLoopBackOff
[2025-11-12T02:14:40Z] autoscaler: desired=80 -> 220 -> 70 (within 2m)
```
Jia Chen: looks like sudden input burst plus autoscaler policy with very short cooldown is thrashing.
Irina K: we’re seeing a driver mismatch alert on ~40% of nodes from the last provider driver patch. Some nodes report mixed driver versions. That could explain increased OOMs on warmup. I recommend pinning new nodes off the recent driver set and scaling pool with older known-good image.
Maya R: first priority: reduce customer impact. Options: (A) freeze autoscaler min/ max to stabilize capacity, (B) disable automatic scaling and manually scale to safe value, (C) route traffic to fallback quantized model. Which is fastest?
Leon Patel: fastest is (B) + (C). Disable autoscaler, set nodepool replicas to a higher steady count, and push the inference router to route hot requests to quantized model-qa (lower mem). I can trigger router edit.
Maya R: @Leon go ahead. Irina, coordinate nodepool change.
Irina K: running commands now:
```
# temporarily disable cluster autoscaler
kubectl scale deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --replicas=0
# scale nodepool to 120 nodes (was 30)
gcloud beta compute node-pools update runtime-pool --num-nodes=120 --region=europe-west1
```
Irina K: note: scaling takes ~3-6m, but will stop the oscillation.
deploy-bot: deploy job queued: routes/update-hotpath -> quantized-model-qa (rollout strategy: immediate) by Leon Patel
Leon Patel: pushing route change:
```
PATCH /config/route
{ "route":"/v1/generate","model":"quantized-model-qa","conditions": {"path_prefix":"/hot"}} 
```
Leon Patel: rolled out to 20% -> 100% over 2 minutes.
Jia Chen: confirm quantized model runs with lower memory and no special driver expectations. Logs look cleaner for those pods.
Maya R: monitoring metrics: 10m ago 503s spiked to 8%; after route change latency dropped for hotpath, overall 503s down to 2.1%, p95 latency still elevated ~12s but trending down.
Support Lead: heads-up — informing affected customers in eu-west. Status page draft:
"We are investigating elevated errors and latency in eu-west affecting some real-time inference requests. Mitigations are in progress."
Maya R: safety step: add blocking config to prevent new model uploads hitting runtime-serving in eu-west until we stabilize.
Irina K: also isolating nodes with driver mismatch:
```
kubectl label nodes node-0abc bad-driver=true
kubectl cordon node-0abc
kubectl drain node-0abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Irina K: working on a rolling replace with the pinned image.
Jia Chen: root cause hypothesis: (1) mixed GPU driver + new kernel on subset of nodes -> increased allocation failures, (2) autoscaler cooldown too short causing scale oscillation -> resource fragmentation -> CrashLoopBackOff cascade.
Maya R: OK, immediate reconstruction: autoscaler off, manual nodepool scale to stable capacity, route hot traffic to quantized fallback. Next: rollback any recent runtime agent changes that changed memory strategies? Jia, any recent agent changes?
Jia Chen: pushed driver-aware allocator change yesterday to prod canary; can roll back to previous release. Rolling back the allocator patch on canary first.
Leon Patel: rollback done on canary, will queue prod if metrics warrant. Also creating emergency canary for the non-quantized model so we can restore later.
Maya R: customer impact note: approx 7% of real-time API tokens in eu-west returned 500/503 during the 02:14–02:28 window. No data loss, only latency/errors. Dedicated customer X reported timeouts; bridging with Account Exec.
Support Lead: I’ve opened support ticket #34219, customers X and Y alerted, sent automated status update via status.redwood.ai/incidents/3351239876
incident-bot: Incident timeline entry created (3351239876) — runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/realtime-hotpath-brownout
Leon Patel: temporary alert suppressors set for OOM flood alerts to avoid alert fatigue while we stabilize.
Maya R: handoff plan: I’ll stay 30m for verification, then handing to Leon for next 2 hours. Leon, accept pager.
Leon Patel: ack, taking over pager at 02:34Z. Will monitor until stable and schedule postmortem. Please leave any notes here.
Irina K: follow-ups: 1) force-replace nodes with mixed drivers 2) tweak autoscaler policy: increase cooldown to 300s, require 3 consecutive readouts before scaling, 3) add preflight check for driver/kernel compatibility in node rollout pipeline.
Jia Chen: runtime follow-ups: 1) revert allocator change if driver-aware path is flaky 2) improve OOM early-detection metric for pod startup 3) add automatic fallback routing when X% of new pods fail start
Support Lead: posting public status update now: "Mitigations in place; traffic rerouted to lower-memory model; we are seeing error rates decline. More updates soon."
Maya R: notes for postmortem: timeline, autoscaler policy parameters, node image/driver rollout, allocator change; impact per customer & token counts, mitigation steps taken and TTL to revert. Assign owners.
Leon Patel: owner list — Jia runtime (root cause), Irina infra (node pipeline), Maya incident lead, Leon follow-up & reliability.
Maya R: thanks all. closing loop: current metrics stable for 6m, errors down to baseline. If we get new flap, re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
Leon Patel: adding retrospective doc to the incident folder and will schedule 1h postmortem within 48h.
deploy-bot: status: route rollback scheduled if error rate rises above 3% for 5m.
Maya R: handing off formally to Leon. glhf.
Leon Patel: taking charge — monitoring. final note: keep support updates on cadence 15m until fully resolved.
